summary:
As a Software Engineer, I build products across frontend, backend, and automation with a focus on clarity, performance, and maintainability. My daily stack spans React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, Python, FastAPI, Rust, MongoDB, MySQL, and Docker, so I can move comfortably between interfaces, APIs, and systems.

Since Sep 2025, I have been working at Revel Healthtech in the healthcare domain, and over the past year I have been improving scheduling, manage visits, call logs, outreach, clinical team tools, search, navigation, and release quality. Across client work and public repositories, I have shipped 35+ products spanning healthcare, fintech, e-commerce, DeFi, developer tooling, and open-source experiments. I care about clean architecture, fast user experiences, and codebases that stay easy to extend.

experience.description: Since Sep 2025, I have been building healthcare product experiences at Revel Healthtech. Over 7+ months, I have focused on making clinical and operations workflows faster, clearer, and more reliable across scheduling, visits, call logs, outreach, search, and navigation.
achievements: Stabilized healthcare workflows across manage visits, scheduling, skip-appointment flows, call logs, outreach filters, and clinical-team screens.
Improved grid view behavior, search box UX, route flicker handling, and step navigation so care teams can move through the app with less friction.
Added automated test IDs and a pre-push hook to strengthen QA, catch regressions earlier, and make release validation more reliable.
Consolidated repeated bug fixes into shared flows to reduce duplication and keep the frontend easier to maintain across adjacent healthcare features.

highlights.title: Healthcare workflow reliability
details: Refined visit management, scheduling, outreach, and skip-appointment screens
Reduced friction in call log and clinical team workflows
Kept the UI predictable for care-coordination tasks

highlights.title: Release readiness and QA
details: Added automated test IDs to support stronger regression coverage
Introduced a pre-push hook for cleaner release validation
Grouped common bug fixes to avoid repeated implementation patterns

experience.description: At RecruiterFlow, I worked as a Frontend Developer, focusing on building reusable components and developing web applications with cutting-edge features. These applications were utilized by thousands of users in their daily routines.
achievements: Redesigned the application form, which is used by more than 1 million people every week. Implemented React similarly to how Meta does it, by injecting it inside the webpage instead of building the entire page with React. This solution significantly increased the speed of the website.
Implemented OpenAI and Bard APIs to automate text writing. Added the speech-to-action feature to enable users to perform actions using voice commands.

Worked on upgrading the Frontend libraries in our very large project with a lot of dependencies. Achieved 100% uptime and zero bugs in production by upgrading chunks of libraries at a time, starting with Node and React. Received praise from the CTO for this accomplishment.

Integrated RF-GPT into our SaaS product, which helps recruiters automate tasks such as email writing, job description creation, and call logs. This feature enhances their workflow by generating screening questions, saving them significant time and effort.

highlights.title: Test Infrastructure & Coverage Expansion (550+ Tests)
details: Took ownership of setting up and expanding the frontend testing ecosystem
Introduced TypeScript for better type safety and scalability
Integrated Jest and React Testing Library (RTL) for robust unit and integration testing
Wrote 550+ test cases, achieving high coverage across critical features

highlights.title: AG Grid Optimization & Bundle Chunking (~45% Faster Load Time)
details: Refactored large data-heavy modules using code-splitting and dynamic imports, significantly reducing initial load size
Optimized AG Grid rendering and state updates, resulting in a ~45% improvement in page load and render times for large datasets
Leveraged techniques like virtualization tuning, memoization, and selective column rendering to minimize unnecessary re-renders
Collaborated closely with the backend team to implement efficient pagination and data shaping strategies

experience.description: In my six months of work, I worked on an enterprise application aimed at providing pre-developed web app templates without the need for coding. Through this experience, I gained valuable insights into professional web development practices and industry standards.

I've worked as a freelancer on React web applications. One project I'm particularly proud of is the PVP Collage site, which I developed as a freelance project. It's a fully responsive website built using Next.js, Tailwind, and JavaScript. You can view the development link here: https://pvpcollage-loni-webapp.vercel.app/

projects.name: Credaryn
projects.description: Open-source trust infrastructure for issuing and independently verifying authentic business documents across digital PDFs and physical paper.
projects.details: Seals PDFs with standards-compatible PAdES signatures, carries signed claims onto paper as machine-readable seals, and verifies both through one normalized result model without requiring a cloud service.

projects.name: Narrator
projects.description: A published research project and local-first PDF-to-audiobook system with a restartable, seven-stage generation pipeline.
projects.details: FastAPI and SQLModel persist job and artifact state in SQLite so interrupted work can resume. The pipeline uses Docling for document conversion, Kokoro for local speech synthesis, optional ElevenLabs/Sarvam cloud TTS, optional Sarvam OCR for Indian-language documents, and FFmpeg for audio mastering and packaging.

projects.name: GID-128
projects.description: A compact, sortable 128-bit identifier format with Rust-backed JavaScript/TypeScript and Python packages.
projects.details: Uses a 48-bit millisecond timestamp and an 80-bit monotonic entropy tail, stores canonical IDs in 16 bytes, and provides a 22-character URL-safe form plus an opaque public projection. Sortable IDs reveal approximate creation order, so the opaque form is intended for external tokens.

projects.name: lipic-js
projects.description: A JavaScript and WebAssembly transliteration library for text inputs, textareas, and contenteditable elements, supporting 27 Indian and South Asian languages.
projects.details: The JavaScript path handles interactive typing and composition events; Rust/WebAssembly accelerates batch work with a JavaScript fallback. Transliteration maps phonetic input into another script; it is not translation.

projects.name: Excalidraw Local
projects.description: A local-first desktop workspace for Excalidraw diagrams, built with React, Tauri, and Rust.
projects.details: Adds tabbed documents, native open/save dialogs, drag-and-drop, autosave, session recovery, Mermaid import, and PNG/SVG/Excalidraw exports. Local files and recovery snapshots remain distinct so recovery does not silently overwrite a saved document.

projects.name: ag-grid-open
projects.description: A TypeScript-first wrapper and extension layer for AG Grid Community with optional Rust/WebAssembly performance paths.
projects.details: Separates core, advanced, and WASM packages, with React examples, worker-based paths, parity checks, and repeatable benchmark scripts. Performance results are operation-specific local snapshots and should not be generalized to every grid workload.

projects.name: Code-EL Platform
projects.description: A local-first coding-practice platform with 200 DSA problems, an in-browser editor, and containerized execution in six languages.
projects.details: Uses Monaco for editing and Docker for isolated test execution across JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, C++, and Rust. Submission history is stored locally for a single user.

projects.name: Local Resume Matcher
projects.description: A local-first research toolkit for comparing resume-to-job matching methods and inspecting ranking behavior.
projects.details: Runs replaceable local model adapters, compares rankings with labels and a lexical baseline, and processes local PDF/TXT inputs. Scores are experimental rubric outputs, not calibrated probabilities or recommendations; the tool is not for employment decisions.

projects.name: CloudRAID
projects.description: A multi-cloud deployment platform with a CLI, control plane, operations dashboard, cost service, and provider adapters.
projects.details: The private case study covers AWS, GCP, and Azure provisioning, desired/observed-state reconciliation, rollback, health evaluation, operator-driven failover for prepared targets, and automatic failover for eligible multi-target AWS/GCP deployments after health thresholds are met. Optional Cloudflare routing is available; provider and workload support varies, and some source layouts need project-specific edits.

projects.name: MUSUMA CSP Portal
projects.description: A multi-tenant business-management platform for inventory, orders, customers, financial tracking, analytics, and ecommerce workflows.
projects.details: The private project spans a React/TypeScript web client, Express/MongoDB backend, Electron desktop distribution, and Docker deployment. Tenant scope and authorization belong in backend queries and writes, not only in UI filtering.

projects.name: Provenance
projects.description: A local-first desktop app for finding and reviewing text reuse in academic assignments.
projects.details: A Tauri/React interface uses separate Rust crates for text normalization, exact and modified matching, common-text handling, and evidence reports. It supports pasted text plus digital TXT, Markdown, PDF, and DOCX; similarity is evidence for human review, not proof of plagiarism. OCR is outside the current product scope.

projects.name: LitLens
projects.description: A local-first textbook digitization pipeline that turns page images into structured Markdown and PDF output.
projects.details: Uses local vision-language models for detection, cropping, preprocessing, parsing, quality evaluation, assembly, and persistence. The same Python pipeline supports single-page, batch, and watched-folder workflows through CLI and Gradio interfaces.

projects.name: rh-mi-icon-data
projects.description: An on-demand Material Symbols delivery system for React that generates only the icons an application uses.
projects.details: A CLI reads a versioned icon registry, generates local assets or components, and works with a small React runtime. The registry can be served through jsDelivr; generated assets can also be self-hosted.

projects.name: VS Code Extension Manager
projects.description: A VS Code extension for exporting and importing extensions and settings across VS Code, Cursor, and VSCodium.
projects.details: Provides a sidebar for selecting extensions, detects editor CLIs, skips already-installed items, and reports install progress and cancellation. Settings are handled as JSONC; imported configuration should be treated as untrusted input.

projects.name: LAN Chat
projects.description: A peer-to-peer desktop chat app that discovers users on a local network and exchanges messages without a central server.
projects.details: A Rust daemon handles mDNS discovery and direct TCP messaging, while an egui client communicates with it over JSON on a Unix-domain socket. The separation keeps networking independent from the UI and supports multiple local instances.

projects.name: ROHO Blockchain
projects.description: An experimental Rust proof-of-work blockchain implementation focused on consensus, transaction validation, and peer-to-peer synchronization.
projects.details: The README describes BLAKE3 mining, Schnorr signatures over secp256k1, a UTXO ledger, persistent state, and network synchronization. This is an implementation project, not a claim of production cryptocurrency readiness.

projects.name: codivex-mcp-server
projects.description: A local code-search engine exposed through MCP, with Rust indexing and search components, a CLI, and a desktop UI.
projects.details: The workspace separates indexing, search, embeddings, shared code, MCP server, and Dioxus UI crates. Its README includes deployment, security, IDE setup, client compatibility, and performance-testing guides.

projects.name: QuillFix
projects.description: A macOS menu bar app that corrects grammar and spelling in selected text using a local MLX model.
projects.details: Built in Rust with a local model download and app-bundling workflow. Local inference keeps selected text on-device; the full MLX build requires the macOS Metal toolchain.

projects.name: SciNotepad
projects.description: A responsive scientific notepad that evaluates equations as users type and supports variables, history, and a math-symbol palette.
projects.details: Expressions ending in '=' are evaluated with mathjs; keyboard controls let users accept or dismiss results. The app also includes scientific functions, matrices, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader support.

projects.name: AI Question Paper Solver
projects.description: An Expo mobile app concept for answering uploaded question papers using supplied reference books and LLMs.
projects.details: The README describes authentication, credit plans, question-paper uploads, and a planned Razorpay purchase flow; payment integration is currently mocked. No live demo is listed.

projects.name: Can I Eat
projects.description: A web app for looking up packaged food in India and understanding ingredients, nutrition, allergens, and dietary compatibility.
projects.details: Searches products by name, brand, or ingredient and presents label information with health indicators and alternative suggestions. The README does not describe this as an AI product or list a live demo.

projects.name: Algo Visualizer
projects.description: An interactive learning app for visualizing common data structures and sorting algorithms.
projects.details: Includes arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, trees, and bubble, selection, insertion, quick, and merge sort visualizations.

projects.name: Rust Web Scraper
projects.description: A Rust web-scraping application with an Axum API, SQLite history, and a user interface.
projects.details: The documented POST /scrape flow uses Firecrawl to fetch Markdown from a URL and caches the result; GET /history returns stored scrape records. A Firecrawl API key is required for that provider path.
